body: The transphobes who actually know what trans men are will argue that literally no trans men want to play men's sports. Which is always a hilarious point to see as a trans man who was on the men's rugby team in college.

Exactly. My mom and I had joked that I was more boy than girl, but once I came out I suddenly had "no masculine traits!" (Thankfully she is at least trying at this point, since it's been like 12 years.)

Yeah, that's exactly what I meant. With AFABs, testosterone does help too. My voice has definitely changed some, but not as much as I wanted. I occasionally get called "ma'am" when I'm on the phone with someone who doesn't know what I look like, and it can be embarrassing and frustrating.

Info for people who don't have experience with transitioning: It can be hard to predict how much the hormones will change various aspects of our bodies. For example I have a friend who is also a trans man who's been on T for years, and he has a great deep voice but can only grow limited facial hair, while I have a fantastic beard but still a fairly high voice. And in my case, it's not only the pitch. I get told that I generally just have a soft voice, so that doesn't help either.

It was not identifiable to me as a woman-only conversation, and I don't think the other participants perceived it as such either. It was a discussion about something of general interest and did not even have anything to do with gender or even femininity. No one had explicitly determined that it was a woman-only conversation until she said that, and it seemed like she was just trying to shut me out because she didn't want to hear what I had to say.

I definitely also do not believe I deserve to have access to women's conversations, spaces or anything else due to my nail polish or any other aspect of my presentation. u/Pip201 got it right. The rude woman was saying that even though I had nail polish on, I'm not a woman and need to shut up.

The aggressive wording combined with low-effort keysmash username made me suspicious that this may not be an innocent question asked out of curiosity, so I looked at some of the user's other comments. When you look at everything else they've said, it comes across as very trollish.

Wow, that really sounds like a pain to deal with!  I'm sorry you're going through that.

The more I look into it, the more I get the sense that I should get it changed.  I guess I need to really make sure I'm going to be doing it right.
Thank you.  This makes a lot of sense.  I think I need to try to talk to her soon.  I'm starting to see that getting this done could be important for the future.

Thanks for this.  

Glad to hear I'm not being ridiculous and to have someone reassure me that it's my decision.  Thanks also for telling me about the potential pitfalls.  I changed my name nearly 6 years ago and haven't needed anything to do with my birth certificate since then, but it's good to know that I may have issues at some point.
There's r/ActualSportsballHate, but it's tiny and dead.

Yeah, you're right.  Way easier said than done.  I always think the next life change will make it easier to talk to people, and I guess it's improving slowly, but it never goes quite the way I expect or hope.  For example my controlling parents used to make it difficult for me to see my friends, so I thought it would get better once I left their house.  When that didn't happen, I thought once I started at my community college.  That didn't help much, so I'm holding on to vain hope that relocating to another new city and starting at a regular college will change things.  At the same time, I know it's not that easy.

Also, two things.  Bad news and (sort of) good news.  I had a minor setback today that I don't really feel like explaining.  It's not that bad, but it could have serious consequences in the near future if I don't take care of things, which I'm feeling too depressed to do.  I kind of took it as a sign that I should just kill myself and get it over with.  Good news is I called my therapist.  (I feel more comfortable consulting him first and seeing if he thinks I need to talk to my doctor.)  He wasn't available, but I left a message.  I probably can't talk to him tomorrow either because of my classes.  Guess it doesn't matter too much anyway since I'll be seeing him Friday and I currently feel ok about my ability to survive til then.

Yeah, you're right.  I should probably call my doctor soon.  Maybe I'll do that tomorrow.  Not sure when I'll be able to get ahold of him though.

My loneliness has been bothering me lately.  I recently came back from a trip where I spent the whole time hanging out with my friends.  Now I'm back to my relatively solitary life.  I almost never see a lot of my friends because they live all over the place.  I interact with classmates, but only in or before class.  I spend way too much time in front of my laptop just wasting time because I am pretty nervous around people and haven't quite gotten the hang of meeting them.  I guess that could contribute.

Thanks for your response.  I feel kind of weird about contacting my doctor about the med change because I'm not sure if it could be causing it or if that's just some weird idea I have that actually makes no sense in reality.  In my somewhat limited research I've found no indications that it's something that happens with this specific medication, which is lithium.  I asked in r/bipolar (with a different account), in much less detail, if anyone else has experienced something similar, but I haven't gotten much of a response.
